clue.text: Sadly lost the wind, it is very light

indicators.note: sadly here suggests the words have come to grief and been knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A mournful remark that the breeze has dropped, followed by an observation about something weightless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' signals an anagram of LOST THE WIND; the definition is the whole closing statement, describing the fluffy seed down of a weed.
explanation.definitionFit: The downy seed tufts of a thistle are so weightless they float on the breeze, hence a byword for lightness.

clue.text: Fruit attached to the trunk

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit fixed to a tree trunk, or perhaps to a travelling chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose hips are the red fruit of the rose, and the hip joints sit at the base of the human torso.

clue.text: Give help to one easily duped, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for a gullible person is to be taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: a sucker is a gullible person, easily fooled

explanation.surface: Aiding a gullible person, according to what people are saying.
explanation.definitionFit: To succour is to bring aid or relief to someone in distress.

clue.text: Calm and send to sleep

explanation.surface: Soothe someone until they doze off.
explanation.definitionFit: A lull is a quiet spell, and to lull a child is to soothe it into slumber.

clue.text: Many felt irritated and abandoned

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
to have itched is to have felt an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: A crowd of people became annoyed and were left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ditched something is to have dumped or discarded it.

clue.text: Objective question of identity in new homicide case

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words new homicide case

explanation.surface: Detectives on a fresh murder file ask who the victim was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' is the grammatical case: this question word is the object form of 'who'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar names the object form of the interrogative pronoun for asking about a person's identity.

clue.text: Suit for the naval officer

parts.note: a suit of cards is one fourth of a pack of cards, and that name is also the raised rear deck of a warship kept for officers

explanation.surface: Tailoring a uniform for a navy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing, but it is one of four suits in a pack, a fraction of a pack.
explanation.definitionFit: On a warship the raised after part of the upper deck was reserved for officers.

clue.text: Playing the market-or just thinking about it?

explanation.surface: Is someone investing in stocks, or merely musing?
explanation.definitionFit: Risky investing in shares hoping for gains is one sense; idle conjecture or theorising is the other.

clue.text: Not the best form of travel

definitions.text: Not the best form of travel

parts.words: Not the best form of travel
parts.note: reads as a complaint about a mode of transport, but means the cheaper tier of rail ticket, or a runner-up rating

explanation.surface: A grumble about an uncomfortable way of getting around.
explanation.definitionFit: Trains offer a cheaper standard tier below first, and the phrase also means inferior.

clue.text: Description of an eternity ring?

parts.note: a circular band has no stopping point, which suits a ring symbolising everlasting love

explanation.surface: A jeweller describing a ring given as a token of lasting love.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes on for ever is perpetual, like a circle with no end point.

clue.text: Get straight an argument over privileges

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the quarrel above the privileges in the grid

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or heated quarrel
rights are entitlements or privileges

explanation.surface: Settling a dispute about entitlements.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in order is to rectify or sort them out.

clue.text: Gives us directions for Customs?

parts.note: taken as written
E for east and S for south are compass points
E for east and S for south are compass points

explanation.surface: Someone asks for guidance on getting through the border's customs hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs' suggests the border post, but it means habits or usages; 'Gives' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Usages, conventions and practices are the habits people follow.

clue.text: Just a piece of water

explanation.surface: Only a small lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere as adjective means nothing more than; as a noun it is a lake or pond.

clue.text: Figure the mob rush out to see

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of mob rush are thrown out of their normal order

explanation.surface: Watch the crowd charge out to see a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric shape: a parallelogram with four equal sides.

clue.text: It can be a source of pain when the sun is up

definitions.text: It can be a source of pain

indicators.note: up in a down clue tells us the words sun is are written bottom to top

explanation.surface: Headaches strike when the sun climbs high in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SUN IS upwards to read SINUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflamed air cavities in the skull cause headaches and facial ache.

clue.text: Glance shows a novice in fault

indicators.note: in places the learner letter within the flaw

parts.note: a defect is a flaw or fault
L for learner is a novice driver's plate

explanation.surface: A quick look reveals a beginner's error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glance' is the verb of a ball glancing off, not a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow that glances off is turned aside, as a shot is diverted.

clue.text: Seats of learning, perhaps

parts.note: seats of learning usually means universities, but here means the furniture pupils sit at in class

explanation.surface: A phrase for universities and colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolroom furniture where pupils sit to write and study.

clue.text: Frosted look seen when I'm in debt?

indicators.note: in puts the contraction within the colour of debt

parts.note: being in the red means owing money
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone looks frosty when they find themselves overdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: RED stands for debt, from the red ink of a bank statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Rime is hoar frost, so something rimed is coated in ice crystals.

clue.text: The boy's in a whirl

explanation.surface: A lad is in a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The boy's' reads as 'The boy is': a lad's name, then a swirl of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddy is a pet form of Edward, and a swirling current of water or air.

clue.text: A noble look

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord in the House of Lords is one; to peer is to gaze closely.

clue.text: Gets the flavour of sweets, so there!

explanation.surface: A child enjoys candy and taunts a sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucks!' is a British schoolchild's jeer of triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: One draws a lolly's taste by mouth; as a taunt it is a playground cry of defiance.

clue.text: Lies, in an open sort of way

definitions.text: Lies, in an open sort of way

parts.words: Lies, in an open sort of way
parts.note: lies seems to mean tells untruths openly, but means lying down spread out

explanation.surface: Someone tells barefaced fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretching out with limbs spread wide is lounging carelessly.

clue.text: Behave shiftily before embarking on the deal

explanation.surface: A card sharp acts suspiciously before dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: To act evasively is one sense; mixing the cards before dealing is the other.

clue.text: Work girls came out in lumps

indicators.note: in places the work within the girls

parts.note: dolls is dated slang for girls
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Female workers broke out in a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came out' is a link joining wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumps of soft food served with a spoon are big blobs.

clue.text: Dishing out for a party

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of dishing are tipped out and rearranged

explanation.surface: Serving food at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively celebration or knees-up.

clue.text: Players in form

explanation.surface: Actors in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The actors in a production; and a mould or shape.

clue.text: Two articles for a goddess

parts.note: the definite and indefinite articles of English grammar
the definite and indefinite articles of English grammar

explanation.surface: A pair of grammatical words name a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Thea or Theia is a Titaness of Greek myth, mother of the sun.

clue.text: Dog-food?

explanation.surface: A tin of pet food.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese breed of fluffy dog; and slang for grub.

clue.text: Bird in difficulty

explanation.surface: A bird in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading sandpiper; and a tangle or problem.

clue.text: Marxist lark, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests lark could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A communist's caper.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of Marx, the philosopher behind communism.

clue.text: Let Jack be seen to supply a military presence

explanation.surface: Raise the Union banner to show troops are here.
explanation.walkthrough: The Union Jack is the British flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally to display the national ensign; idiomatically to make one's forces visible.

clue.text: They do turns on the printers

definitions.text: They do turns on the printers

parts.words: They do turns on the printers
parts.note: sounds like entertainers performing, but means rotating type discs in old typewriters

explanation.surface: Performers do acts at the print works.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotating discs with petal-like spokes carrying characters in old printers.
